name: Radiation-proof seed capsule
subtitle: seeds that survive years in deep space

effects.effect: certain proteins turn glassy inside cells and let them survive drying out

effect: certain proteins turn glassy inside cells and let them survive drying out
how: A crew on the way to Mars cannot carry mass for shielding, and seeds sent ahead sit for years in cosmic radiation that breaks their DNA faster than a dormant seed can repair it. Tardigrades carry a protein that wraps DNA and physically blocks the damage; a seed given that gene, dried into a glassy state and sealed in a thin steel capsule, carries its shielding inside each cell rather than as cargo. The same capsule serves as a backup seed bank on Earth.
obstacle: A protein that coats DNA may also get in the way of the plant reading it, so growth and protection have to be traded off.
why: Dsup protects cultured cells; whole seeds across years of cosmic rays is untested.
real: Dsup reduces radiation-induced DNA damage in human cells and has been expressed in tobacco pollen (UV-B) and reportedly rice, but no Dsup transgenic seed, dried glassy state or sealed-capsule space-storage demonstration was found.
